transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-11 09:15 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Azura Head of Platform), Tom Reyes (Azura Security Engineer), Ellen Park (Azura PM), Ravi Shah (Azura Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Quick run through of POC metrics, retention settings, and audit log requirements. 
- Clarified SOC 2 artifacts needed and potential data residency questions. 
- Agreed next steps: share docs, confirm retention windows, schedule compliance deep dive.

Topics: SSO / SAML, Audit logs (export/schema), Data retention and redaction, SOC 2 artifact mapping, Observability for pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Alright hi everyone, thanks for joining. we're on the 11th, quick hello. um liam and i from Redwood, and then Azura team, hi. can everyone say name and role quick?
[00:08] Priya: Priya Nair, head of platform.
[00:11] Tom: Tom Reyes, security.
[00:13] Ellen: Ellen Park, product.
[00:15] Ravi: Ravi Shah, compliance.
[00:17] Liam: Liam O'Connor, solutions eng. quick agenda: retention + logs, soc2 ask, and a short results review from last week's ingestion tests.

[00:35] Priya: sounds good. we ran the throughput run last thursday, latency looked fine. our main open worries are retention and who can see tokens in logs, so we wanna make sure audit trail is solid.
[00:47] Maya: yeah totally. quick note, during the pilot you're on Redwood hosted with a private vpc link — right? or did you switch to dedicated? i thought you were on dedicated trial.
[00:56] Priya: currently it's hosted w/ private peering, not Dedicated — we kept it hosted to move faster, but we might need dedicated if logs need to be fully customer-controlled.
[01:06] Tom: i'd like to understand where the audit logs live, retention defaults, and export options. and also whether kyc pii or PHI tokens end up in logs— we need redaction.

[01:20] Liam: good call. so, current default audit log granularity is request-level metadata plus an optional request/response body if you enable full payload logging. we recommend keeping bodies off for PHI. you can enable structured event logs and we support export to S3 or to a syslog/SIEM via our log-forwarder.
[01:35] Tom: export to S3 is ok, but Azura wants streams into Splunk. can we do a push?
[01:42] Liam: yes we have a small connector we can enable to push events to Splunk HEC. we'll need a token and an endpoint. note the connector currently ships with truncated request ids for privacy but full ids can be toggled for enterprise.

[01:58] Ellen: quick question on retention: minimums / maximums? we were thinking 30 days, but compliance may ask for 90. also will redaction be applied before logs leave the environment?
[02:09] Maya: retention is configurable, default 30 days for pilot, up to 365 for enterprise. redaction rules can be applied at collection time using regex or by leveraging our PII scrubbing pipeline. two caveats: if you're on hosted the raw logs are stored encrypted at rest in our storage; if you require on-prem or fully customer-managed storage we can for Dedicated/Private add support but it's a different contract.

[02:34] Tom: how's key management handled? can we bring our own KMS to encrypt at rest?
[02:38] Liam: yes for Dedicated and Private you can BYOK (bring your own key) via KMS/HSM integration; hosted has our managed KMS by default but we can offer a customer key for enterprise with some additional attestation.

[02:55] Priya: SOC 2 — what artifacts will Redwood provide for the pilot? we need a mapping to our vendor assessment template.
[03:01] Maya: we can share our SOC 2 summary report excerpt and control mappings. full SOC 2 report requires an NDA typically but we'll provide the summary and the relevant control IDs for the controls around access, encryption, logging, and incident response.
[03:17] Ravi: ok can you include retention controls and evidence of log exports? the security questionnaire also asks about RBAC — can you show role definitions?
[03:24] Liam: yes we have RBAC with roles: viewer, operator, admin, auditor. auditor role is read-only on audit logs and can't see request/response bodies by default. we can also do service accounts with fine-grained permissions.

[03:40] Maya: quick results review from last week's test — you ran 10k concurrent messages through the streaming api. latency p99 was 230ms per token for the short prompts, costs came in around our expected pilot profile. liam, do you have the numbers?
[03:53] Liam: yeah, the p50 was 78ms p95 140ms p99 230ms. token cost per 1k was roughly $0.42 with our current batching enabled, but if you switch quantized variant the cost drops ~30% with a small quality delta.

[04:15] Priya: quality's fine for now, main blocker is audit detail and retention policy. Tom wants to demo the actual logs.
[04:21] Tom: yes i'd like to see a sample event and confirm PHI masking. we also want to test the SIEM push end to end.

[04:29] Liam: ok i'll generate a synthetic log sample with PHI indicators and show how the scrubber works. note: because transcriber sometimes mislabels thing, but the scrubber uses token-level heuristics plus regex so some edge cases need manual redaction list.

[04:45] Ellen: on data residency — Azura is US only for now, but some regional rules may pop up. does Redwood support region pinning for hosted?
[04:51] Maya: yes we can pin to specific cloud regions in hosted; for strict residency dedicated or private is the better path since you can control where the storage live.

[04:58] Ravi: one callout — our legal team wants audit logs kept for a rolling 365 days but with automated deletion of request bodies after 30 days. possible?
[05:06] Liam: yes that's a common pattern: keep event metadata for 365, strip bodies after 30. we can set lifecycle policies on S3 exports or configure TTL on our managed storage.

[05:18] Tom: what's the retention policy API look like? can we change it via console or do we need an API call?
[05:23] Maya: both, console for quick changes and infra-as-code via API for GitOps. we'll share the retention API doc.

[05:31] Priya: also want to verify alerts — if someone escalates an incident, how fast are audit logs available for postmortem? real-time or near real-time?
[05:38] Liam: logs are streamed near-real-time; export latency to external systems depends on connector but typically < 60 sec. for internal tracing we keep higher fidelity for 24 hours before aggregating.

[05:55] Maya: ok let's do a runbook: we'll send SOC 2 excerpt, sample logs, and policies. we'll also do a live demo of the Splunk push next Tuesday if that works.

[06:05] Priya: Tuesday works, can we do morning pacific?
[06:08] Maya: sure. liam will do the demo and tom will validate.

[06:15] Ravi: quick question — does Redwood provide signed audit log hashes for non-repudiation?
[06:20] Liam: we have log signing for enterprise, can provide SHA256 chain hashes on exported files, and attestations in the enterprise package.

[06:32] Ellen: final q — redaction: can we define custom redaction lists (like account numbers) via API?
[06:37] Maya: yep custom redaction lists and rules can be uploaded via API or UI. we'll include an example.

[06:44] Tom: thanks, if you can show the sample and we'd like to see the actual SIEM integration in a dev Splunk instance to verify field mapping.
[06:51] Liam: noted, we'll set up a dev Splunk endpoint and share creds out-of-band.

[06:58] Maya: any other concerns? otherwise we'll recap next steps.
[07:02] Priya: none from me.
[07:04] Ravi: all good.
